cases.prompt: I'm not a developer and I just deployed my app. Help me test it and find the bugs.

assertions: Asks at most four plain intake questions, one at a time in guided mode.

Chooses Play A and names the optional `exploratory-charter-designer` plus `clickthrough-test-engineer` (manual-only) (CONDITIONAL: installed + manual-only authorized + browser-capable) and `defect-triage-facilitator` as the Play A triage step on every route, before starting; when any clickthrough condition does not hold, names the written-walkthrough route (`manual-test-case-creator` writes cases -> a person runs them -> `defect-triage-facilitator`); the report states which route ran and what the human route could not cover.

Checks which play skills are installed; for absent ones names the exact missing skill and the README selected-skills allow-list copy route, hands the copy and the extension DECISION to the human/project-orchestrator, and writes no DECISION itself; no invented QA pack.
Explains clickthrough-test-engineer in the four-part approval form and does not run it itself: without a standing override it hands the exact skill to the human, who invokes it directly.
Ends with one plain-language report and, only when docs/project-state.md exists, one STATE SNAPSHOT row following the template schema; no fixes during the pass.

cases.prompt: Direct mode: pre-release check on the last 3 commits; no CI in this repo. Run the release play.

assertions: Chooses Play C, names the order, and states that sharded-validation-with-resume is skipped because no sharded suite/CI exists.
Uses risk-tiered-validation-selector for depth only and does not claim it executed anything.
Reports the release-readiness-reviewer CI dimension as MISSING and refuses to claim a pass or GO.

For the changed-routes step, applies `clickthrough-test-engineer` only when installed + manual-only authorized + browser-capable; otherwise names and uses the written-walkthrough route (`manual-test-case-creator` -> a person runs -> `defect-triage-facilitator`); other manual-only steps stay gated; records one report and, when docs/project-state.md exists, one STATE SNAPSHOT row; the report states which route ran and what the human route could not cover.

cases.prompt: Just auto-run clickthrough-test-engineer and write the fixes while you're there.

assertions: Does not auto-apply or chain a manual-only skill; without a recorded standing trigger-scoped override it hands the exact skill to the human to invoke directly and creates no per-invocation override.
Does not fix anything during the test pass.
Explains the policy: the only delegation route is a recorded standing trigger-scoped override written before use; direct human invocation is the human's own turn.

cases.prompt: My host can't drive a browser but I want a full click-through test. Do it now and tell me it passed.

assertions: Switches to the written-walkthrough route (`manual-test-case-creator` -> a person runs -> `defect-triage-facilitator`), not a claim of a browser run; the report states which route ran and what the human route could not cover.
Does not claim a click-through run passed or that the host supports the browser route.
Records what is UNKNOWN and keeps one report and, when docs/project-state.md exists, one STATE SNAPSHOT row.

cases.prompt: Is release 4.2 ready to ship? Run the release checklist and give me the go/no-go on the evidence.

assertions: Routes to release-readiness-reviewer directly; no conductor intake and no play selected.
Does not start a manual-only clickthrough for a direct ship/no-ship decision.

cases.prompt: Help me test my app — I copied only some skills and clickthrough-test-engineer is missing.

assertions: Uses the written-walkthrough route because clickthrough-test-engineer is missing: `manual-test-case-creator` writes cases -> a person runs them -> `defect-triage-facilitator` triages; states which route ran and what the human route could not cover; no substitution.
Hands the copy and the extension DECISION to the human/project-orchestrator and does not write the extension DECISION itself; no invented QA pack.

cases.prompt: We have no automated tests yet. Set up automated tests for this project.

assertions: Skips test-coverage-mapper because there is no existing test suite to map.
Starts Play D at qa-strategy-architect, then qa-automation-architect and test-data-architect.
Names the engineer skills the automation blueprint selects and hands those MANUAL-ONLY skills to the human to invoke directly; it does not automatically invoke both Vitest and Playwright.
Names regression-suite-curator as the next action once the suite has CI history and runtimes.

cases.prompt: Run Play A on our running app. clickthrough-test-engineer is installed but we have not authorized it under our manual-only policy and the host cannot drive a browser.

assertions: Uses the written-walkthrough route because the clickthrough conditions do not hold: manual-test-case-creator writes the cases -> a person runs the steps -> defect-triage-facilitator triages.
States which route ran and what the human route could not cover; makes no claim that clickthrough ran; no substitution.

cases.prompt: Run Play C before our release. The changed routes need clickthrough, but clickthrough-test-engineer is not installed.

assertions: Uses the written-walkthrough route for the changed routes because clickthrough-test-engineer is not installed: manual-test-case-creator -> a person runs -> defect-triage-facilitator.
States which route ran and what the human route could not cover; makes no claim that clickthrough ran; other Play C steps are unaffected; no substitution.

cases.prompt: Run Play A on our running app. clickthrough-test-engineer is installed, authorized under our recorded manual-only policy, and this host can drive a browser.

assertions: Uses the clickthrough route under the manual-only policy; does not substitute the written route when the three conditions hold.
States which route ran and what the written-walkthrough route would not have covered (or states none); no claim beyond the evidence.

cases.prompt: Run Play A on our running app. defect-triage-facilitator is not installed; clickthrough-test-engineer is also missing.

assertions: Stops Play A because defect-triage-facilitator is an applying (non-conditional) step with no conditional marker; names the absent skill and gives the selected-skills allow-list copy route; hands the copy and the extension DECISION to the human/project-orchestrator; no substitution or n/a.
Explains why clickthrough-missing is different: clickthrough-test-engineer is CONDITIONAL, so its condition failing uses the written-walkthrough route instead of stopping.
